title: Creating & Managing Databases
description: Create databases, configure templates (template0, template1), set encodings (UTF8), and configure collations.

data.text: In PostgreSQL, a **database cluster** is a single running PostgreSQL server instance that manages multiple independent databases. Each database is an isolated namespace containing its own tables, schemas, and catalogs.

data.title: Creating a Production Database with UTF8 and ICU Collation
data.code:
CREATE DATABASE production_app
    WITH 
    OWNER = app_admin
    ENCODING = 'UTF8'
    LC_COLLATE = 'en_US.UTF-8'
    LC_CTYPE = 'en_US.UTF-8'
    TEMPLATE = template1;

data.text: These three words are used loosely in conversation but mean different things, and mixing them up is a classic interview miss. A **cluster** is one running server on one machine (one `PGDATA` directory). A **database** is a fully isolated catalog inside that cluster — you cannot query across databases in a single statement. A **schema** is just a namespace *inside* one database, and you can join across schemas freely.

rows: One server, one data directory, one port
A namespace for tables, views, functions, types

data.text: Templates: Where New Databases Come From

PostgreSQL does not create an empty database from nothing. `CREATE DATABASE` **copies an existing template**. By default that is `template1`, so anything you install in `template1` (extensions, helper functions) is inherited by every new database. `template0` is a pristine, read-only copy you should use when you need a non-default encoding or collation.

data.title: Creating Databases With the Right Template
data.content: Copy from template1 to inherit setup; from template0 to change encoding or collation.
data.code:
-- Standard database, inherits template1 (extensions, custom functions)
CREATE DATABASE app_development
    OWNER    = app_admin
    ENCODING = 'UTF8'
    TEMPLATE = template1;

-- Change collation or encoding: must use template0
CREATE DATABASE app_prod
    OWNER      = app_admin
    ENCODING   = 'UTF8'
    LC_COLLATE = 'en_US.UTF-8'
    LC_CTYPE   = 'en_US.UTF-8'
    TEMPLATE   = template0;

-- PostgreSQL 15+: ICU collation chosen per database
CREATE DATABASE app_icu
    OWNER      = app_admin
    ENCODING   = 'UTF8'
    LOCALE_PROVIDER = 'icu'
    ICU_LOCALE = 'en-US'
    TEMPLATE   = template0;

rows: Always `UTF8`. Converting later requires a dump/restore.
Controls sort order and character classification (`ILIKE`, `UPPER`). Decided at creation, effectively immutable.
PG 15+. More consistent, versioned collations across operating systems.
Set `false` for a migration target you do not want clients hitting yet.
Per-database cap, useful to protect a small instance from one tenant.

data.title: Listing, Sizing, and Renaming Databases
`CREATE DATABASE` Cannot Run Inside a Transaction
data.text: Because it copies a template, it must run as a top-level statement. That is why migration tools wrap everything *except* database creation in a transaction, and why `DROP DATABASE` has a `WITH (FORCE)` option in PG 13+ to terminate active connections.

data.title: Provision a Fresh Environment
data.description: Practise the provisioning path you would script in a real project.
steps: Connect to `postgres` and create a role: `CREATE ROLE app_admin LOGIN PASSWORD 'secret';`
Create `app_development` owned by `app_admin` with `UTF8` encoding from `template1`.
Connect to it with `\c app_development` and confirm the encoding with `SHOW server_encoding;`.
Try `CREATE DATABASE test COLLATE "C" TEMPLATE template1;` and explain the error — then fix it with `template0`.
data.expectedOutcome: A database you can connect to, with the correct encoding and owner, created from the right template.

items.question: Can I write a query that joins tables across two databases?
items.answer: Not directly. A single connection is bound to one database. Use `postgres_fdw` foreign data wrappers, `dblink`, or logical replication to consolidate the data — or keep related tables in the same database under different schemas.

items.question: Why does changing collation require a new database?
items.answer: Collation affects how indexes store and compare text, so it is recorded at the cluster/database level. You must create a new database and migrate the data.

items.question: What is `template0` for?
items.answer: It is a pristine read-only template that lets you choose a different encoding, collation, or locale than `template1`, and it is also useful for restoring a dump that specifies a different encoding.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cluster → database → schema are three nested scopes; new databases are **copied from a template**, not created empty.
Use `template0` whenever you need a non-default encoding or collation; use `template1` to inherit extensions.
Always provision with `UTF8`; prefer the ICU locale provider on PostgreSQL 15+.
`CREATE DATABASE` cannot run inside a transaction block, which affects how migrations are scripted.
data.takeaway: Aim to answer with the template detail: "new databases are cloned from template1, so I use template0 when I need a different locale".
